## Statement

A global effective sample size is a scalar function of the weight distribution, so it does not encode where in covariate space the support lies or whether the supported region is relevant to the decision contrast. Reporting is demonstrably incomplete in practice: of 117 oncology MAICs reviewed by Farinasso et al. 2025 (doi:10.1016/j.vhri.2025.101088), only three fulfilled all NICE recommendations and the distribution of weights was among the least reported items. The claim that software reports ESS alone and never computes contrast-specific influence is too strong: cpaic, an unreleased development package on GitHub that is not on CRAN, already exports a weight panel with effective sample size, entropy efficiency, weight variation, concentration and residual balance, plus an edge influence function for a named treatment contrast. What remains missing is a definition set agreed across packages and the support-geometry diagnostics that no package computes: region-specific ESS, convex-hull distance, density-ratio and optimal-transport cost, out-of-distribution maps, and balance on omitted moments.

## Why it is open

Effective sample size is the squared sum of the weights divided by the sum of their squares, so it is invariant to where the weights sit in covariate space; the same value can come from a broad shifted distribution or from a decision-relevant subgroup with no source support at all. Balance is conventionally reported on the moments that were matched, which is tautological, while balance on the omitted moments is the informative check and is usually skipped. Because no body owns the definitions and at least three competing ESS calculations for population adjustment have been proposed, two analyses of the same evidence can report incomparable numbers, and no empirical knowledge accumulates about which diagnostic values predict bias.

| [Three new methodologies for calculating the effective sample size when performing population adjustment, 2024](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12874-024-02412-1) | Proposes three competing ESS calculations for population adjustment, evidence that no single ESS definition is fixed across packages and publications. The literature auditor retrieved this at title and venue level only. |
| [cpaic (development version), commit 9d150e9](https://github.com/choxos/cpaic/commit/9d150e9cad88f2e6fbcd94dbb92c3dee3b7c2dca) | Unreleased development package on GitHub, not available from CRAN. Exports a weight-quality panel (ESS, entropy efficiency, weight variation, concentration, residual balance) and an edge influence function for a named treatment contrast, documented as approximate for multi-arm networks. |

:::

## Probable solution or research direction

Standardize and extend what exists rather than specify a panel from scratch: agree one definition set across packages, starting from the multi-metric weight panel and contrast-specific influence already implemented in cpaic, and add the support-geometry diagnostics no package computes, namely region-specific ESS, convex-hull distance between source and target support, density-ratio and optimal-transport cost, out-of-distribution maps, and balance on omitted as well as fitted moments. Require the agreed panel in publications and submissions. Evaluate each member of the panel in simulation for its ability to predict realized error, and drop the ones that only describe the fit.

## What this project measured

**Study `studies/DIA-02-the-whole-weight-panel-is-a-multiset-functional`, run and decided
against a rule registered before the run.** 48 cells, 2000 replicates each, 96,000
replicates. Nine diagnostics: the five reported panel members, all symmetric functions of
the weight multiset, against four candidates that read position as well as weight.

**The manipulation.** Two source populations remove the same mass at the same threshold on
exchangeable standard normal coordinates and differ only in which coordinate carries the
hole: the one that modifies the treatment effect, or a purely prognostic one. The first is
biased by **+0.01639** on the target marginal risk difference; the second by **-0.00009**,
which is zero to five decimal places. Material error, meaning the transported effect wrong
by more than 0.03 absolute risk, occurs on **0.106** of replicates in the first and **0.005**
in the second, against **0.003** with no hole at all.

**Result on the registered primary: refuted.** Section 7 registered the AUROC of each
diagnostic against material error *within* the modifying-hole arm. There the best panel
member reaches 0.574 (`max_weight`) and the best geometric candidate 0.592 (`ess_region`), a
gap of 0.018 against a registered materiality of 0.10. By the registered rule the panel
discriminates as well as the geometric diagnostics, and the proposition is refuted.

**Result on the study's own control: confirmed, emphatically.** Section 8 registered a
separate check, that at matched multisets every panel member must be numerically identical
across the two support arms. Read as a discrimination task over 16,000 replicates, **every
panel member sits within 0.005 of chance** (`max_weight` 0.505, `ess_kish` 0.502,
`entropy_eff` 0.501, `top_share` 0.500) with a standard error of 0.005, while `ess_region`
separates the two arms at **1.000** and optimal-transport cost at 0.726. The blindness is
measured, not merely unrejected.

**The disagreement is the finding.** Within one arm every replicate shares one hole
placement, so the only thing varying is sampling noise and the outcome asks which replicate
drew a bad sample. A concentration measure answers that about as well as anything. The
proposition is about comparing analyses at *different* placements, and only the cross-arm
comparison varies it. The registered primary outcome was the wrong measurement for the
question the study was built to ask, and the study's own control was the right one. That is
recorded rather than repaired by relabeling the control as primary after the fact.

**The refuting sentence in the design fails.** Two analyses differing by 0.016 in bias were
built at a panel matched to 2% in an ordinary covariate law, not a contrived one, so the
invariance bites in practice and not only in principle.

**Two of three controls failed, and the failures cost three quarters of the grid.** The
matched-multiset control failed wherever a modifier's second moment was left unmatched, by up
to a 0.908 relative difference, because dropping that moment breaks the coordinate symmetry
the manipulation rests on. The null control failed at `dim8/moderate`, where MAIC's own
sampling error exceeds the 0.03 threshold on **0.288** of replicates with no support hole at
all, and at `dim3/moderate` at 0.021. The source size had been registered from a noise floor
measured at the middle of the grid, and the middle is not the worst corner. This is the same
defect IDN-05 documented, of a threshold set below its own measurement noise, and it is worth
naming twice because such a floor reads as a finding. The analysis drops failing strata on
the controls' own evidence rather than on the results, leaving 12 of 48 cells and 24,000
replicates.

**The comparability half, quantified for the first time.** Three published ESS definitions
computed on identical data disagree by a median factor of **1.55**, a 90th percentile of
**3.50**, and a maximum of **15.48**. The complaint that two analyses of the same evidence
can report incomparable numbers had never been given a size.

**What this does not answer.** Four limits, three of them live. `hull_gap` is a geometric
diagnostic and is blind anyway, at 0.503, because it maximizes over coordinates and both arms
remove an identical wedge; reading position is not sufficient if the reading is then
aggregated away. `balance_omitted`, registered as the cheap comparator most likely to
overturn the headline, was never given anything to see: the cells where it has content are
exactly the ones the matched-multiset control eliminated, so the comparison the design wanted
did not run. `ess_region` requires choosing a region, and the choice here is the effect
modifier's upper decile; that is available to an analyst, since MAIC already requires naming
the modifiers, and it is not knowledge of where the hole is, but it is a choice a decision
rule would have to register. And no diagnostic here is calibrated: separating two placements
is not a threshold.

## Verification

::: {.verification-trail}
**Verdict.** Partially addressed. Auditors disagreed and the disagreement was evidence-bearing on both sides. Reopened by the full-text reading: 1 finding from 1 paper survived both the reader and an independent second reviewer, so the verdict moves from unverifiable to partially-addressed, on a single finding.

**The source titled this.** "ESS reported alone and overlap diagnostics are not standardized" The title says software reports effective sample size alone, which the audit judged too strong given an implemented multi-metric weight panel and contrast-specific edge influence.

**The source said.** "Overlap is summarized by a single effective sample size, which cannot show the geometry of covariate support, where the analysis is extrapolating, or whether the supported region is relevant to the target contrast. The definitions and displays of overlap, ESS, extrapolation and modifier-balance diagnostics also differ between packages and publications, so two analyses of the same evidence report incomparable numbers."

**What was wrong with it.** The claim was unattributed in the source and is now sourced: the literature auditor supplied Farinasso et al. 2025 (doi:10.1016/j.vhri.2025.101088) for heterogeneous and incomplete diagnostic reporting, and a 2024 paper proposing three competing ESS calculations (doi:10.1186/s12874-024-02412-1) for the non-standardization of ESS itself. GPT-5.6 Sol read cpaic at commit 9d150e9 and found a multi-metric weight panel and contrast-specific edge influence already implemented, so the ESS-only claim fails there; the two auditors disagreed on whether the entry as written was supported or overstated, and the weaker reading is published here.

**Dissent.** literature dissented (open): This entry is source_unsourced; I found real references that support it. Farinasso et al. 2025 scoping-reviewed 117 oncology MAICs and reports that only 3 fulfilled all NICE DSU recommendations and that among the least reported items was the distribution of weights, with mean sample-size reduction 44.9%. That is direct published evidence that diagnostic reporting practice is heterogeneous and suboptimal. Independently, a 2024 BMC Med Res Methodol paper proposes three new ESS calculations for population adjustment, which is itself evidence that no single ESS definition is fixed across packages and publications. I found no PAIC package or publication reporting local (region-specific) ESS, optimal-transport cost, convex-hull distance, out-of-distribution maps, balance on omitted moments, or influence alignment between IPD study edges and the decision contrast; those remain absent, though absence found by search is weaker evidence than the reporting review. codex dissented (overstated): C4 through C7 follow directly from ESS = (sum w)^2 / sum(w^2): the same weights can be reassigned to different covariate locations without changing ESS, despite different local support and contrast relevance. The claim that software reports only ESS and never computes contrast-specific influence is already false for cpaic at the requested commit. It exports `weight_diagnostics()` with ESS, entropy efficiency, weight variation, concentration, and residual balance, plus `edge_influence()` for a named treatment contrast. The latter is documented as approximate for multi-arm networks. Local ESS, convex-hull distance, density ratios, and transport costs are complementary diagnostics requiring careful definitions and validation, not established replacements for ESS. Cross-package standardization and fuller support-geometry diagnostics remain open.

## How the evidence falls in time

8 papers in the reviewed corpus bear on this problem, published 2012 to 2024. Partial progress is on the record, and later work still calls this open. Both belong in view.

This problem is **recurrent**: three or more papers spanning at least eight years assert it independently. Sustained restatement by authors who mostly do not cite each other is the strongest evidence this reading can offer that a gap is real rather than one group's framing.

::: {.table-scroll}

| Year | Says | Paper |
|---|---|---|
| 2012 | confirms it is open | Sample size and power considerations in network meta-analysis |
| 2018 | confirms it is open | Quantifying and presenting overall evidence in network meta-analysis |
| 2019 | confirms it is open | Alternative Weighting Approaches for Anchored Matching-Adjusted Indirect Comparisons via a Common Comparator |
| 2019 | confirms it is open | Population Adjustment Methods for Indirect Comparisons: A Review of National Institute for Health and Care Excellence Technology Appraisals |
| 2019 | confirms it is open | Using Matching-Adjusted Indirect Comparisons and Network Meta-analyses to Compare Efficacy of Brexanolone Injection with Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitors for Treating Postpartum Depression |
| 2022 | partly addresses it | Geometric approaches to assessing the numerical feasibility for conducting matching-adjusted indirect comparisons |
| 2023 | confirms it is open | A Critical Appraisal of Matching-Adjusted Indirect Comparisons in Spinal Muscular Atrophy |
| 2024 | confirms it is open | Response to "Letter to the Editor Regarding 'Matching-Adjusted Indirect Comparison of the Long-Term Efficacy Maintenance and Adverse Event Rates of Lebrikizumab vs. Dupilumab in Moderate to Severe Atopic Dermatitis'" |
